Let's be honest here: After the enormous burst of popularity Voat got after the Reddit admins went full retard amidst the Pao drama, many of the new users no longer use Voat and may have returned to Reddit, use imageboards instead, or whatever it may be.

Problem is, their accounts are still around, and there's lots of them. Take v/Gaming for instance, which officially has almost 60,000 subscribers but (as far as I can tell) never anything remotely close to a triple-digit number of actual users online.

Apart from distorting the impression of how active/popular individual subverses and also Voat in general are, this also might cause issues for smaller and younger subverses that have no chance of rising to the top because they can not possible get the same tens of thousands of "frozen" subscribers that the older subverses have.

Naturally there is a counter-argument against this in the form that people who come back to Voat after a long time will find their entire subscription list wiped clean, but I think if you put a reasonably long time of absence as a requirement for this to happen (say, six months of inactivity), you can be fairly certain that the respective user is not coming back any time soon. Plus, said users always can look up the subverses they frequented via their comment history.

Any other opinions on this?
Should Voat automatially de-subscribe accounts from subverses if the account has not been used for several months?
No objection to changing the number used for display and ranking from "subscribers" to "active subscribers", but it's not nice to fuck with users' settings in absentia.

Comtinuing this line of thought why not display both? It would be a neat statistic to see.

At the same time I would question the amount of value a change like this would bring. No doubt the calculation involved for every user of every subverse done at whatever set inverval would involve a fair amount of processing. Voat already has infaststructure and speed issues, so to pile more on top for little gain seems illogical despite how nice the feature may be.

I don't think fake subscriber points are any more important than any other fake internet points. What is going to keep people interested in a sub is content. A sub with big numbers and no new content isn't going to keep folks who are otherwise active on the site.
